clue.text: Doctor No's at place to trade in 007's vehicle?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mart is a market, a place where goods are traded
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about where James Bond might trade in his car, with Dr No making an appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like Bond's villain's title but is the anagram signal: NO'S AT rearranged gives ASTON.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond famously drives this British sports car make in several films, so it is his signature vehicle.

clue.text: Use artillery for cover

definitions.meaning: to bombard a position with big guns
a hard outer casing or husk protecting something

explanation.surface: An instruction to fire big guns to keep the troops protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombarding with artillery is the verb sense; the hard casing of an egg or nut is the noun sense.

clue.text: Group of stars gathering at address

indicators.note: gathering means taking something in, so the constellation surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Orion is the hunter constellation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A constellation clustering at some location in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a location but is a formal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An address in the sense of a formal speech delivered to an audience is a synonym.

clue.text: Fail to find motorway covering Scottish island

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, covering it

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
Islay is a Hebridean island famous for whisky

explanation.surface: A traveller who cannot locate the road that runs over a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: ISLAY is an island off the west coast of Scotland, known for its whisky distilleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to put it somewhere and then be unable to locate it.

clue.text: Organist somehow dressing down

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A church musician getting a scolding of some sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe reprimand or telling-off is an informal synonym for a harsh scolding.

clue.text: Stupid African despot for the listener

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda
otic means relating to the ear, the organ a listener uses

explanation.surface: A foolish African tyrant performing for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the listener' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it gives OTIC, meaning of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish or senseless behaviour is described with this adjective, a synonym for stupid.

clue.text: Lout with money just about fit for purpose

parts.note: a rough is a rowdy, violent person
and means together with
the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A yob with cash in hand, barely suitable for the task.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crude but adequate for the job is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Visit our amazingly talented musicians

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters are thrown into surprising disorder

explanation.surface: An invitation to come and see a gifted band.
explanation.definitionFit: Masters of an instrument with exceptional skill are called by this Italian plural.

clue.text: Indiana Jones perhaps loathes a corgi barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The film adventurer hates a yapping royal dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' seems to describe the dog but means crazy; corgis are the breed linked with the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The film hero is a professor who digs up ancient relics, an example of this profession.

clue.text: The ultimate feature of some games

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The final characteristic of some sporting contests.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end or final thing.

clue.text: It's more alarming admitting if one means to break up

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: scarier means more frightening
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something said to be even more frightening if it lets things fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or machine that loosens soil or breaks up a surface such as a lawn or road.

clue.text: Every Russian in sporty car to gad about

indicators.note: in places the other pieces within the car abbreviation

parts.note: GT stands for gran turismo, a sporty car
every means all
Ivan is a stereotypical Russian name

explanation.surface: Every Russian zooming around for fun in a sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam around in search of pleasure is a synonym for gadding about.

clue.text: Little chap beginning to thrive before long

indicators.note: beginning to points at the initial letter of the next word

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A small boy who starts to grow quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is a British informal word for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a very small person, often a little boy.

clue.text: Colourless football team switching pair at the back

indicators.note: the final two letters of the team name trade places

parts.note: Albion is a common team name, e.g. West Bromwich Albion or Brighton and Hove Albion

explanation.surface: A washed-out football side changing its two defenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair at the back' sounds like defenders, but it is the last two letters, O and N, swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or animal lacking pigment is white or pale, with no colour.

clue.text: Sweet shot?

definitions.meaning: a throw or shot hitting the centre of a target

explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British mint candy and a perfect hit on the centre of a dartboard share this name.

clue.text: A kiss cut short to show affection for one that may be related

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is taken off

parts.note: to neck is to kiss
to dote is to show great fondness

explanation.surface: A brief kiss to show fondness for someone who may be a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'related' suggests family but means told, as a story is related.
explanation.definitionFit: A short story is something told or recounted, which is what related means here.

clue.text: Note time absorbed in handicraft

indicators.note: absorbed in means taken inside the other piece

parts.note: crochet is a craft of hooked needlework

explanation.surface: Someone noting how time disappears while doing needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical note worth one beat, called a quarter note in America.

clue.text: What's brought from food shop before jolly

indicators.note: before puts the shop ahead of the second piece

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen
jolly means very in British speech, as in jolly good

explanation.surface: Items carried out of a delicatessen ahead of a cheerful event.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignment of goods carried to a customer is what is brought.

clue.text: Trace viewer regularly introducing Top Gear driver

indicators.note: introducing means bringing another piece inside
regularly takes every other letter of the next word

parts.note: the Stig is the anonymous racing driver on the BBC motoring show Top Gear

explanation.surface: A TV viewer following the trail of a mystery Top Gear driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace' looks like a verb but is the noun: a faint remnant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small remaining sign or remnant of something is a trace.

clue.text: Hospital cutting top-class medication that's on the rise

parts.note: U means upper class in British usage

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the other pieces

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine

explanation.surface: A hospital rationing high-quality drugs while prescriptions climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Going up a slope or climbing is a synonym for rising.

clue.text: Love potion makes Duke of Edinburgh tango with the queen

parts.note: Phil is short for Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh
T is tango in the NATO alphabet
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A royal romance aided by a magic drink, with the Duke dancing with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tango' looks like the dance but is T in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic drink to make someone fall in love, an alternative spelling of philtre.

clue.text: Removing vice from China perhaps is a hard problem

indicators.note: removing says the following word is taken out of the longer piece

parts.note: china is an example of a tea service

explanation.surface: Stamping out vice in China is a tough challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is crockery: a tea set.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky puzzle or brain-teaser is a hard problem.

clue.text: Bridge players perhaps unpleasant creatures when losing the lead

indicators.note: losing the lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: beasts are nasty animals or people

explanation.surface: Nasty card players going behind in a bridge game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a bridge term but is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players sit as compass points; two seats in a session might be called by that direction.

clue.text: Vehicle for 007 damaged slightly evading hit

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bond's car takes slight damage while dodging a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' looks like a car but is a film starring Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle is also a film that showcases a star; this 1987 film starred James Bond.

clue.text: Plans advanced in certain days in Rome

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Ides were days in the Roman calendar, such as 15 March
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Plans being brought forward to particular days in ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts or schemes for action are synonyms for plans.

clue.text: See 24
For Frenchman, extremely small lock

parts.note: très is French for very

explanation.surface: A tiny curl of hair described by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' sounds like an extreme-letters signal, but it is the French word for very.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock of hair is a curl or strand, the same as a tress.

clue.text: Characters showing relief from disturbed rest slept round about

indicators.note: round means surrounding the other piece
disturbed means troubled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A disturbed sleeper finds relief from turning over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' sounds like comfort but is raised printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing from raised type produces characters in relief on the page.
